project_info.title: Tehran Subsidence Monitoring using Sentinel-1 InSAR

reference_point.reason: Assumed stable reference in Alborz foothills

corrections_applied.purpose: Not needed due to high data quality

limitations: All velocities are RELATIVE to the reference point in north Tehran
Absolute velocities require GNSS calibration (not available in this study)
Positive values indicate stability relative to reference, not true uplift
District boundaries are approximate (Voronoi-based around known district centers)
3 districts have low prediction confidence (R² < 0.5): District 3, District 2, District 5
Imam Khomeini and Payam airports are outside InSAR coverage - values are estimated
Sentinel-1 ascending data was not included in this analysis
Temporal coverage is limited to 12 months (2024)

interpretation.critical_zones: Districts District 19, District 16, District 20, District 10, District 18 in southern and southwestern Tehran show severe subsidence (-48 to -24 mm/yr)
interpretation.stable_zones: Northern and eastern districts (1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 12) appear stable or positive relative to reference
interpretation.positive_values: Values > 0 mm/yr likely reflect: (1) relative stability compared to subsiding south, (2) possible natural uplift, (3) small residual systematic errors
interpretation.population_risk: Approximately 1,277,995 people (14.7%) live in high-risk districts
interpretation.infrastructure_risk: Metro stations in Districts 10, 16, 17, 18 are in critical condition
interpretation.main_cause: Groundwater over-extraction is the primary driver of subsidence in southern Tehran

recommendations: Install continuous GNSS stations in critical districts for absolute calibration
Expand InSAR analysis to include ascending orbit data
Integrate groundwater level data for causal analysis
Develop early warning system for critical infrastructure (metro, airports)
Conduct field surveys to validate InSAR results
Use higher resolution DEM for improved topographic correction
Extend temporal coverage to multi-year analysis (2020-2024)
